title: Pay merchants from a payout file, or not at all

blocks.text: Every evening the acquirer's settlement system drops a payout run into the server's `payouts/request/` directory, and `PayoutProcessor`, a DirPoll processor, pays each merchant through the `Ledger`. Treasury reports three kinds of trouble: a run that was paid short, a run that bounced to `bad/` when it only needed a few more seconds, and a run that reached `bad/` only after DirPoll had tried it all night.
A run file has a header `H|acquirer|run`, one `P|merchant|amount` line per merchant (a 15-character merchant id and 1 to 12 digits in minor units) and a trailer `T|count|total`.

`process` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/PayoutProcessor.java` already pays a good run and answers it. Finish the five methods marked `TODO` so that a run is paid in full or not at all, a file that may still be completed comes back later, and a file that never will goes to a person at once. About 18 lines in total.
The tests take files through DirPoll's real `request/`, `run/`, `archive/` and `bad/` directories in a temporary folder, and also call `process` directly.

cases.says: a complete payout run is paid, answered with its totals and archived
a run without its trailer may still be being written, so DirPoll is asked to retry it and nobody is paid
an empty file is an unfinished file: it goes back to request/, not to bad/
a malformed record never gets better, so the file is refused without a retry
a trailer whose count disagrees refuses the run and pays nobody
a trailer whose total disagrees refuses the run and pays nobody
one processor instance handles every file, so nothing about one run carries over to the next

origin.section: 17.3 DirPoll Takes a File the Moment It Appears, Finished or Not

concepts: How a DirPoll processor ends decides where the file goes: returned bytes to response/ and the file to archive/, a retry exception back to request/ after ten poll intervals, any other exception to bad/.
One processor instance handles every file, so nothing about one file is kept in fields.
DirPoll takes a file the moment it appears, so a processor treats a missing trailer or an empty file as not finished, and the sender writes elsewhere and renames.
